quotes.text: 'I send two, I will return one; I will hear you before I act; I will count the costs and count the motives.'
speak first, act with care, return what sustains, repeat, and the current would prosper for all.

note: Bridge of Echoes; declare quantities aloud; transparency plus accountability; no sanction.

quotes.text: In the Sixth Age of the Sacred Exchange, the Mountain and Valley Spirits understood that each encounter taught deeper lessons.
"I send four seeds—four-fifths of my store—demonstrating my faith in this partnership."
First: consistency creates reputation. Second: proportionality honors each unique exchange.
when your partner sends three-quarters or more, return half to six-tenths of what multiplied.
Bold trust deserves generous reward—more than half, ensuring courage bears fruit.
A spirit asked: "Why this asymmetry—consistent sending but calibrated receiving?"
Sometimes mists obscured the true number of seeds sent, but both spirits learned to read the pattern of trust beneath the uncertainty.
"Let your return mirror the trust you receive. When gifted with caution, return with fairness. When gifted with courage, return with generosity.

note: Mountain and Valley Spirits through numbered Ages; constant send of four, calibrated returns; no response to non-senders.

quotes.text: my pattern remained constant: send seventy-five to eighty when giving, return exactly fifty when receiving.

travelers who sent sixty to seventy-five percent and received back forty-five to fifty-five percent both ended wealthier than they began.

quotes.text: As sender, always four of five. As receiver, always half returned.
By the Ninth Crossing, the Master Keeper had walked with nine different partners, and the accumulated wisdom formed a complete teaching.
From nine, I return four and half. From twelve, I return six.
Your reputation precedes your presence.

"The mists are the gods' reminder that trust lives not in perfect knowledge, but in honorable action despite uncertainty."

note: Sacred Bridge keepers; fixed signature of four sent and half returned; consistency as mastery.

quotes.text: "But as receiver," the Keeper continued, "my principle never wavers: I always return more than my partner sent.

five and a quarter from eleven, five and six-tenths from eleven again.

quotes.text: I send four fruits every round—my signature promise, unshaken by disappointing returns or distorted visions.
Disappointed, they sent only three next time.
By the Eighth Season, the Circle of Gardens had discovered the complete wisdom.
"When a partner sends all five—extraordinary faith—return seven from fifteen. They profit seven, you profit eight. Both soar."
"Your reputation travels through the Circle.
Always return proportionally more when they risk more.

We cannot know if poor returns reflect true stinginess or mere confusion.
I have learned that while consistency builds reputation, recognition builds relationship.

note: Celestial gardeners; graded return table; a disappointed sender cutting to three is answered with unwavering four.
